To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the uptake hydrogenase (hupL) of Nostoc sp strain PCC 7422 is transcribed in both heterocysts and vegetative cells, (b) the hupL transcript is upregulated in response to the shift from non-nutrient to nutrient conditions, and (c) the bidirectional hydrogenase (hoxH) transcript is not upregulated in response the shift from nonnutrient to nutrient conditions

(i) N. muscorom and N. PCC 70102 have a contiguous hupSL, (ii) N. muscom has an hoxFUY gene cluster, and (iii) the hupL transcript is light-dependent and induced approximately 24 h following a shift to nitrogen-fixing growth conditions.

(i) the presence of a hupS gene is not sufficient to induce a bidirectional hydrogenase in filamentous heterocysts; (ii) a hupS-hupL gene arrangement is sufficient to confer H2 uptake in heterocysts; and (iii) a hupL transcriptional induction is not sufficient to confer HoxF activity.

the regulation of the uptake hydrogenase in heterocyst-forming cyanobacteria and the possible role of the bidirectional hydrogenase in the regulation of the nitrogen fixation process.
